title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1965 notes on a Galois theory of motives. Here Grothendieck characterizes the algebraic numbers that can occur as Frobenius eigenvalues of weight 1 ("Q-Weil numbers"). Fix Q in Q*_{>0} and an algebraic λ in C.

The proposition states that the following are equivalent.
(a) Every conjugate λ_α satisfies |λ_α|^2 = Q.
(b) There is a totally real number field K such that K(λ) is K itself or a totally imaginary (CM) quadratic extension of K, and λλ̄ = Q.
(b') Same as (b), with K = Q(a) and a = λ + λ̄ = λ + Q/λ.
(b'') There is a totally real algebraic a, with 4Q − a^2 totally ≥ 0, such that λ^2 − aλ + Q = 0.
(c) Let 𝕂 be the maximal totally real subfield of Q̄ and 𝕃 the unique quadratic extension of 𝕂 that is Galois over Q (the maximal CM field Q^{cm}). Then λ ∈ 𝕃 and λλ̄ = Q.

Proof as written:
- (a)⇒(b''): put a = λ + Q/λ. Its conjugates are a_α = λ_α + Q/λ_α = λ_α + λ̄_α, which are real. λ_α is a root of T^2 − a_α T + Q, and the two roots are λ_α and λ̄_α. These are complex conjugate, so a_α^2 − 4Q ≤ 0.
- (b'')⇒(b'): Q(a) is totally real and λ has degree at most 2 over it. Since a^2 − 4Q ≤ 0, the roots are λ and λ̄, so λλ̄ = Q. On the next page he shows that when λ ∉ Q(a), all λ_α are non-real (a_α^2 − 4Q < 0), so the extension is purely imaginary.
- (b')⇒(b)⇒(c) are trivial.
- (c)⇒(a): complex conjugation is central in Gal(𝕃/Q). Hence λ_α λ̄_α = N_{𝕃/𝕂}(λ_α) = σ_α(N(λ)) = Q.

The next page adds a remark. Every CM field L over a totally real K = Q(a) is generated by some λ with λλ̄ = Q^i for i large: take a root of λ^2 − aλ + Q^i, choosing i so that 4Q^i − a^2 ≫ 0 at every real place. If Q is an integer and a is integral, λ is integral.

This is the standard 'Weil numbers live in CM or totally real fields' lemma. Grothendieck needs it to locate Frobenius eigenvalues of motives over F_q inside Q^{cm} and to define the relevant Galois groups/tori.
errors: In (b'') the condition should be '4Q − a^2 totally ≥ 0' (non-negative), not totally positive. The case a^2 = 4Q, i.e. λ = ±√Q real, must be allowed, and the proof of (a)⇒(b'') only yields ≥ 0. The next page implicitly corrects this by treating a^2 = 4Q separately.
In the equation 'T^2 − a_α T + Q_α = 0', Q_α is a slip for Q (Q is rational).
Minor gap in (b): if λ ∈ K is real, then λ^2 = Q forces λ = ±√Q. This is consistent, but K must then contain √Q. The statement handles this implicitly via 'K(λ) = K'.

ideas.what: Characterization of q-Weil numbers: all conjugates have absolute value √Q iff λ lies in a totally real or CM field with λλ̄ = Q, iff λ satisfies λ^2 − aλ + Q = 0 with a totally real and 4Q − a^2 totally ≥ 0.
ideas.modern_name: Weil numbers lie in CM fields / Q^{cm}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore around Weil, Tate, Honda (Tate's 1968 Bourbaki talk on Honda–Tate theory); exposited in Milne's work on motives over finite fields
ideas.where_published: Standard in Tate, 'Classes d'isogénie des variétés abéliennes sur un corps fini' (Sém. Bourbaki 1968) and later literature

ideas.what: The maximal CM field 𝕃 as the largest Galois extension of Q in which complex conjugation is central (from the previous page); every subfield is totally real or CM.
ideas.modern_name: Q^{cm}, maximal CM subfield of Q̄
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; used by Serre, Deligne, Milne (Weil-number tori, Taniyama group)

ideas.what: Every CM field is generated by a Weil number of weight i for some i (next-page remark).
ideas.modern_name: Existence of Weil numbers generating a given CM field

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct but standard lemma on Weil numbers and the maximal CM field. It is mildly interesting only as early (c. 1965) evidence that Grothendieck placed Frobenius eigenvalues of motives in Q^{cm}, anticipating the Weil-number tori later used by Serre, Langlands–Rapoport and Milne. The mathematics itself is well known.
transcription_corrections: First line: the image reads 'Soit Q ∈ ℚ*,' — the '+' subscript is not clearly visible, though positivity is used.
(b''): the phrase after 'avec' is partly struck and hard to read; 'réel[?]' is doubtful. The image seems to read '4Q − a^2 soit[?] tot. positif'.
'Q_α' in 'T^2 − a_α T + Q_α = 0' is as written in the manuscript (author's slip), not a transcription error.
